g1.label: 1. MLK was born in ___
g1.why: The text says Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta.

g2.label: 2. Entered college at age ___
g2.why: The text says he entered college at the age of fifteen.

g3.label: 3. The boycott started after ___
g3.why: The text says the Montgomery Bus Boycott was started after Parks was arrested.

g4.label: 4. The boycott lasted ___
g4.why: The text says the bus boycott lasted 381 days.

g5.label: 5. The speech was delivered at the ___
g5.why: The text says the "I Have a Dream" speech was delivered at the March on Washington.

g6.label: 6. The Civil Rights Act made discrimination ___
g6.why: The text says the Civil Rights Act made racial discrimination in public places illegal.

g7.label: 7. King was ___ when he won the Nobel Prize
g7.why: The text says King was thirty-five when he won the Nobel Peace Prize.

g8.label: 8. King was in Memphis to support ___
g8.why: The text says King was in Memphis in 1968 to support striking workers.

g1.label: 1. Rosa Parks ___ (simple past passive)
g1.why: A single completed past event takes the simple past passive: ‘was arrested’.

g2.label: 2. The speech ___ (simple past passive)
g2.why: A single completed past event takes the simple past passive: ‘was delivered’.

g3.label: 3. Passengers ___ to sit at the back (past perfect passive)
g3.why: An action true before another past point (the boycott) takes the past perfect passive.

g4.label: 4. The Civil Rights Act ___ (simple past passive)
g4.why: A single completed past event takes the simple past passive: ‘was signed’.

g5.label: 5. MLK Day ___ today (simple present passive)
g5.why: A regular present-day event takes the simple present passive: ‘is celebrated’.

g6.label: 6. King ___ the Nobel Prize (simple past passive)
g6.why: A single completed past event takes the simple past passive: ‘was awarded’.

g7.label: 7. Leaders ___ by Gandhi (past perfect passive)
g7.why: An action true before another past point (King's movement) takes the past perfect passive.

g8.label: 8. His speeches ___ today (simple present passive)
g8.why: A regular present-day fact takes the simple present passive: ‘are still studied’.

g1.label: 1. Separation of people by race
g1.why: ‘Segregation’ is the separation of people based on race, e.g. in schools or on buses.

g2.label: 2. Refusing to buy/use as protest
g2.why: A ‘boycott’ is refusing to buy or use something as a form of protest.

g3.label: 3. Treating someone unfairly by race etc.
g3.why: ‘Discrimination’ is treating someone unfairly because of race, gender, or religion.

g4.label: 4. Fighting for change without violence
g4.why: ‘Nonviolent resistance’ is fighting for change without using physical violence.

g5.label: 5. Against a country's constitution
g5.why: ‘Unconstitutional’ means against the rules of a country's constitution.

g6.label: 6. Deliberate killing of an important person
g6.why: ‘Assassination’ is the deliberate killing of an important person, often for political reasons.

g7.label: 7. Basic rights every citizen should have
g7.why: ‘Civil rights’ are the basic rights every citizen should have, such as the right to vote.

g8.label: 8. A large public meeting for a cause
g8.why: A ‘rally’ is a large public meeting or event to support a cause.
